```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(terroir)
```

## What terroir does

`terroir` pulls climate, weather, vegetation-index, soil, elevation and
agricultural-economics data **for a single geographic point** from many free
sources, behind one uniform contract. You build a request, choose a source, and
get back a tidy, provenance-stamped series.

It is the data-collector member of the ORCHESTRA: a *producer* that feeds
covariates and forcings to downstream modelling. Every source is an
optional adapter, so terroir installs and works with none of the source packages
present (a missing source yields a structured refusal, not an error).

## The registered sources

```{r}
list_sources()
```

Every adapter is **free** -- the data-collector role forbids a paid source
(`register_source()` refuses `free = FALSE`).

## A request

```{r}
req <- geo_point_request(
  lon = 138.6, lat = -34.92,       # Adelaide
  start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-31",
  variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"),
  source = "nasapower"
)
req
```

## Collecting (live)

`collect_point()` performs the download. It is not run here (vignettes build
offline), but the call is simply:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
series <- collect_point(req)
series                 # a geo_point_series: tidy data.table + provenance
attr(series, "provenance")
```

## Offline replay (zero network)

`terroir` ships a small set of recorded fixtures, one per CORE source. Passing
`offline = TRUE` answers a request from the matching fixture with no network
egress at all -- useful for a reproducible pipeline, for a continuous-integration
run, and (with coarsening, below) for a sovereign coordinate that must never
reach an upstream service. A replayed series carries `replayed = TRUE` in its
provenance and keeps the recording's `retrieved_at`, so a consumer can always
tell a cached series from a live one.

```{r}
offline_req <- geo_point_request(
  lon = 138.6, lat = -34.92,
  start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-10",
  variables = c("T2M", "PRECTOTCORR"),
  source = "nasapower"
)
series <- collect_point(offline_req, offline = TRUE)
is_replayed(series)
attr(series, "provenance")$retrieved_at   # the fixture's stamp, not now
head(series, 3)
```

Offline mode needs none of the source packages installed: it reads `.rds`
fixtures and never touches an adapter. When no recorded fixture answers a
request, offline mode returns a structured refusal rather than silently falling
back to the network -- the zero-egress guarantee is absolute. You can point
`terroir` at your own directory of recorded fixtures with
`options(terroir.fixture_dir = "/path/to/fixtures")`, or switch the whole
session offline with `options(terroir.offline = TRUE)`.

A `geo_point_series` is long (one row per date x variable), so plotting it as
small multiples -- one panel per variable, sharing the date axis -- is the
natural way to look at what a collector call actually returned.

```{r, fig.cap = "Adelaide, 1-10 January 2020, replayed from the shipped NASA POWER fixture: daily mean air temperature at 2 m (top) and daily precipitation (bottom). No network call was made to produce this figure."}
vars <- unique(series$variable)
op <- par(mfrow = c(length(vars), 1), mar = c(3, 4, 2, 1))
for (v in vars) {
  sub <- series[series$variable == v, ]
  plot(as.Date(sub$date), sub$value, type = "b", pch = 16,
       xlab = "", ylab = paste0(v, " (", sub$unit[1], ")"), main = v)
}
par(op)
```

Temperature swings from 15.5 to 31.06 degC across the ten days -- a
day-to-day range typical of Adelaide midsummer once a front moves through --
while precipitation is essentially dry (two days record a trace, 0.03 and
0.06 mm; the rest are zero). A collector that returned a flat temperature
line or a wet run of days here would be the signal to distrust the fixture
before trusting anything built on top of it.

## Sovereign coordinates (coarsening)

A grower's exact paddock GPS is sensitive. When a point is flagged
`sovereign = TRUE`, `terroir` coarsens the coordinate to roughly a one-kilometre
cell **before** any upstream call, so the exact location never leaves the host.
Both the raw-requested and the coarsened-sent coordinate are recorded in
provenance -- the host keeps the full record, the upstream service sees only the
coarsened point.

```{r}
sovereign_req <- geo_point_request(
  lon = 138.63124, lat = -34.92871,   # an exact paddock GPS
  start = "2020-01-01", end = "2020-01-31",
  source = "nasapower",
  sovereign = TRUE                    # coarsening on by default
)
sovereign_req       # prints both the raw and the coarsened (sent) point
```

Coarsening is also available for a non-sovereign point via the `coarsen`
argument: a single number rounds to that many degrees of precision (for example
`coarsen = 0.01` for a ~1 km cell), and `coarsen = list(grid = 0.25)` snaps each
coordinate to the nearest quarter-degree grid node. The returned series'
provenance gains `sovereign`, `coarsen_policy`, and the raw-vs-sent coordinates;
the fixed ten-column series schema is unchanged, so a consumer reading those
columns is unaffected.

The returned `geo_point_series` always has the same fixed columns, readable
from the exported schema accessor --

```{r}
geo_point_schema()
```

-- plus a mandatory provenance attribute (source, version, retrieval time,
licence, the exact upstream call). The `unit` column is part of the contract
but is not yet populated by every adapter: `nasapower`, `silo` and `abares`
currently emit `NA_character_` there, while `modis` and `stac` set `"index"`.
`verify_geo_series()` checks the schema and the provenance fields and fails
loudly if either is missing, so a malformed series never flows downstream
silently -- but it does not yet warn on an all-`NA` `unit` column.

## Graceful refusal

If a source's package is not installed, or its free key is unset, you get a
first-class refusal rather than an error:

```{r}
out <- collect_point(geo_point_request(0, 0, source = "not_a_source"))
is_refusal(out)
out
```

## Sources at a glance

| source id | upstream | domain |
|---|---|---|
| `nasapower` | nasapower | global climate + solar (no key) |
| `silo` | weatherOz | SILO 5 km grid, Australia (free email key) |
| `abares` | read.abares | Australian gridded farm economics |
| `modis` | MODISTools | MODIS NDVI/EVI |
| `stac` | rsi | Sentinel-2 NDVI via Planetary Computer |
| `nert` | nert (AAGI-AUS) | TERN soil, soil-moisture, AET, canopy height, phenology (Australia; free key) |

GSODR, geodata (WorldClim + SoilGrids + elevation) and chirps are enrolled in
the ORCHESTRA and land as adapters in a future release.
